newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe approves Airbus 319 to fly with IAE engines.
newsitem.headline: Europe approves Airbus 319 to fly with IAE engines.

text.p: The European Joint Aviation Authorities (JAA) on Wednesday approved the use of International Aero Engines V2524 motors in the Airbus A319 narrow-body passenger jet, Airbus said.
The JAA certified the A319 to fly with CFM International CFM56-5B engines in April.

The JAA's counterpart in the Commonwealth of Independent States, the Interstate Aviation Committeee-Aviation Register, also approved both versions of the A319 on Wednesday, Airbus said in a statement.
International Aero Engines is a five-firm joint venture led by Britain's Rolls-Royce and Pratt and Whitney, a unit of United Technologies Corp.
CFM International is a joint venture between U.S. group General Electric Co and France's state-owned SNECMA.

Airbus is a consortium of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
